# Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) Deep Dive Analysis

Report 049 | Published 2021-02-28 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2021-2-28/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/049.json)

Bond stress, Bitcoin and exchange businesses.

The stimulus timing and income effect were clear successes. The dated SLR-or-QE forecast failed. Exchange-business resilience was partly supported, but mortgage cyclicality and new borrowing complicate the near win-win characterization.

**Coverage:** All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

Omicron emergence reduced protection; booster doses were needed to restore and maintain protection, while three doses retained robust protection against severe outcomes in non-immunocompromised people.

Fed began tapering purchases in November 2021, ended purchases in March 2022 and then raised policy rates; subsequent balance-sheet runoff replaced expansion. This differs from formal yield caps.

Federal funds target increased to 5.25-5.50%; Treasury/MBS holdings continued to decline. This was tightening rather than a permanent low-rate cap.
